# Dossier — Stage 4: independent sources, batches and provider failure

All requirements from stages 1–3 continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §4, §8 and §9 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Many URLs can carry one source: copies, syndicated articles and lookalike domains. A dossier
now says which independent origins stand behind each value, and who has invested in the
company. Researchers submit companies in batches under one shared budget, and research
continues when provider calls fail. There are three idempotent write paths: stage 1's two
and `POST /batches`.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the earlier lists:

5. Spending never exceeds a budget that this specification or the caller sets.

## Lineage header lines

Three header lines (§4, Pages) now carry requirements:

| Header line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Registrant: <domain>` | The domain whose owner publishes the page |
| `Canonical: <URL>` | The page is a copy; the URL is the original |
| `First-Published-By: <domain>` | The page republishes material first published by that domain |

Domains in these lines, and the host of a `Canonical` URL, are normalised as in §4. A page
with no valid `Registrant` line has the host of its own URL, normalised, as its registrant.

## Own pages

A page counts as kind `own` for a company only when its registrant is the company's domain.
Any other page that states `Kind: own` has kind `aggregator` for the selection rule in
`stage-2.md`, and its candidates report `"kind": "aggregator"`.

A page that states `Kind: own` and whose registrant is not the host of its own URL,
normalised, is a **lookalike**: a site presenting itself as a company it is not registered
to.

## Origins

Every page has one **origin**, a domain, taken from the first of these that applies:

1. Its `First-Published-By` domain.
2. When its `Canonical` URL is not the page's own URL, the origin of the page at that URL
   (its **original**), by these same rules.
3. The company's domain, when the page is a lookalike.
4. Its registrant.

A build obtains from a provider each original that rule 2 needs. From the page whose origin
is sought, rule 2 follows at most three `Canonical` URLs in a row. Where it would follow a
fourth, or where no provider serves a page at the URL, the host of that URL takes the place
of the original's origin.

Pages with the same origin are one source, however many URLs, providers or kinds they have.

Candidates gain `origin`, the origin of their page. Each field gains three keys:

```json
{ "value": "Dana Ruiz", "status": "known",
  "citations": [ { "...": "..." } ], "candidates": [ { "...": "...", "origin": "acme-robotics.test" } ],
  "origins": ["acme-robotics.test", "registry.test"],
  "corroborated": true, "corroborated_since": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
```

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates whose value is the selected value,
  sorted ascending. It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when `origins` has two or more entries, otherwise false.
- `corroborated_since` is the time (§8) of the earliest ready build after which the
  selected value has had two or more **standing origins**, or null while it has fewer.
  The standing origins of a selected value are the origins of every candidate with that
  value that any ready build has gathered since the value became the selected value (the
  `learned_at` of its latest history entry, stage 3), whether or not a later build
  gathered it again. A new selected value starts with none. Imported candidates count as
  gathered at the imported `researched_at`. When a stage-3 export is imported, the candidates
  of each of its builds count as gathered at that build's time.

Imported candidates whose export records no origin take the host of their URL, normalised,
as their origin.

For `executives` (`stage-3.md`) and `investors` (below), these keys follow the field's
members. A member's candidates are those with its title and name (`executives`) or with its
name (`investors`).

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates of all members, sorted ascending.
  It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when the candidates of every member have two or more distinct
  origins, and false otherwise, including for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated_since` is the time of the earliest ready build after which every member has
  had two or more standing origins, or null while some member has fewer or the field is
  `unknown`. A member's standing origins are the origins of every candidate of that member
  that the build after which it last became a member, or any later ready build, has
  gathered, whether or not a later build gathered it again. Imported candidates count as
  above.

## Investors

A dossier has an eighth field, `investors`. The `fields` of every response that lists a
dossier's fields hold it, after `executives`, and the feed entries one build adds are
numbered with `investors` last.

For Appendix A, `investors` is a field with the statement phrases `investor`, `investors`,
`led by`, `backed by` and `participated`. Occurrences of the company's name and of these
statement phrases are first taken out of the sentence and separate the words around them.
Of the runs of capitalised words (A.4) joined by single spaces that remain, each not part of
a longer such run, a run of two or more words whose last word is `Ventures`, `Capital`,
`Partners`, `Fund`, `Investments`, `Holdings` or `Equity` is an **investor name**. In an
excerpt that contains an amount (A.4), the run that starts directly after `led by` or
`backed by` and one space is an investor name too, whatever its length and last word:
`Acme Robotics raised $40M in a round led by General Atlantic.` names `General Atlantic`,
and `Acme Robotics is led by Dana Ruiz.` names no investor. An
investor name normalises to the text as the excerpt writes it. Rules 1 to 4 of A.2 apply;
in place of rule 5, an excerpt supports each investor name it contains.

The `value` of a candidate of `investors` is one investor name. A research claim is never a
candidate of `investors`.

An investor name is a **member** when, among the field's candidates, one with that name has
`kind` `own` or `filing`, or those with that name have two or more distinct origins.

In place of the selection rule in `stage-2.md`, the value is the array of the members'
names, sorted by Unicode code point, or null when there is no member. `investors` is `known`
exactly when it has a member, and `unknown` otherwise, in place of the rules that make a
field `known` exactly when the evidence supports a value for it.

```json
{ "value": ["Bluebird Capital", "Northwind Ventures"], "status": "known",
  "true_from": "2024-05-02", "learned_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "citations": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "candidates": [ { "value": "Bluebird Capital", "...": "...", "selected": true }, { "...": "..." } ],
  "origins": ["acme-robotics.test", "dealwire.test", "registry.test"],
  "corroborated": true, "corroborated_since": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
```

- `selected` is true on every candidate whose name is a member, and false on the others.
- `candidates` lists every candidate in the order the selection rule in `stage-2.md` ranks
  them.
- `citations` are, for each member in the order of the value, the `url`, `excerpt` and
  `provider` of every candidate with its name, in rank order.
- A member's `true_from` is the earliest `true_from` that is not null among the candidates
  with its name, or null when all of them are null. The field's `true_from` is the latest of
  its members' `true_from`, or null when the value is null or any member's is null.
- `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values` decides membership from the candidates at `true_at` and
  gives the value, `true_from` and `citations` from them by these rules.

# Dossier — stage 3

A company-profile service: `POST /dossiers` researches a company by its domain in the
background, through Nimble called via WebRouter, and `GET /dossiers/{domain}` returns seven
fields (the six of stage 1 and `executives`), each with the excerpts that support it and every
candidate value the evidence holds. Stage 3 adds change over time: each value carries
`true_from` and `learned_at`, `GET /dossiers/{domain}?as_of=` answers as the service had the
dossier then, `/values?true_at=` what the evidence says held on a date, `/history` each
field's selected values, and `GET /changes` a feed of every change and correction. State is
kept on disk and survives an abrupt stop. Sources that disagree are ranked by a fixed rule (authority, recency, URL, value);
the best candidate is the field's value and the field is `contested`. Researchers use it in
a browser at `/` (list and research form), `/dossiers/{domain}`, `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence`,

"""Page text: header lines and prose (§4 Pages), and the citable sentences of the prose."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re

from .support import collapse_whitespace, split_sentences

_HEADER_LINE = re.compile(r"[A-Z][a-z]+(?:-[A-Z][a-z]+)*:(?: |$)")
_LINE_BREAK = re.compile(r"\r\n|\n|\r")

MAX_EXCERPT = 500


def prose_of(text: str) -> str:
    """The page's prose: everything after the header, or the whole text when it has none."""
    lines = _LINE_BREAK.split(text)
    if not lines or not _HEADER_LINE.match(lines[0]):
        return text
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() == "":
            return "\n".join(lines[index + 1:])
    return ""


def header_of(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The page's header lines as name -> value (the first of a repeated name), up to the first empty line."""
    lines = _LINE_BREAK.split(text)
    header: dict[str, str] = {}
    if not lines or not _HEADER_LINE.match(lines[0]):
        return header
    for line in lines:
        if line.strip() == "":
            break
        name, sep, value = line.partition(":")
        if sep and _HEADER_LINE.match(line):
            header.setdefault(name, value.strip())
    return header


# Wording a page uses to say its figures are filled in by a browser: such a page's plain text
# may differ from what a browser shows once it has loaded.
_DYNAMIC_HINT = re.compile(
    r"real[- ]time|\bload(?:s|ed|ing)?\s+(?:live|dynamically|in the browser)\b|\blive\s+data\b|"
    r"\bjavascript\b|\bdynamically\b|\b(?:update|updates|updated|refresh|refreshes|refreshed)\s+live\b",
    re.IGNORECASE)


def looks_dynamic(prose: str) -> bool:
    """Whether the prose says that parts of the page are filled in after it loads."""
    return bool(_DYNAMIC_HINT.search(prose))

Other pages that state it report `aggregator`, and a lookalike's origin is the company's domain.
- **Origins:** the origin follows the four rules in order. The builder fetches each original a `Canonical` URL needs, follows at most three hops, then uses the host of the next URL. An unserved original also gives its host. Candidates gain `origin`.
- **Corroboration keys (`app/corroboration.py`):** each field gains `origins`, `corroborated` and `corroborated_since`, for scalar fields, `executives` and `investors`. The standing origins are tracked per member and reset when the member stops being one.
- **Investors:** an eighth field after `executives`, with Appendix A rules 1–4 and the investor-name rule. Members, sorted value, `selected` flags, citations, `true_from`, correction/change typing and `/values` follow the spec. The first-round searches now include one `"<Name> investors"` query, 1 unit.
- **Batches:** `POST /batches` is idempotent and validates as specified. A wrong JSON type for `budget_units` is 422. `GET /batches/{id}` is per user, so another user's batch is 404. Builds in a batch draw on one `Pool` and each keeps its own 80 units. Dossiers that already exist cost the batch nothing.
- **Provider failures:** a refused call (5xx or 429) is retried up to four attempts, still bounded by the retry horizon. A refused extract is tried again in a later round. Extracts are given up on only after three refusals with none served. Refused searches are repeated once.
- **Restarts:** a second small file, `running.json`, is written and synced before each call's units are spent. After a restart, every build that was running ends `failed`, immediately. Its fields are left as they were, and its units count in the dossier and the batch. `POST …/refresh` then starts a new build.
- **Upgrades:** stage-1, stage-2 and stage-3 exports import. Candidates without an origin take their URL's host. `investors` is `unknown` in the imported state and in every kept build. The builds are replayed to compute `corroborated_since`.

- Injected provider failures. The retry paths are covered only by the existing `test_retries` unit tests.

**Known gaps and judgement calls**
1. A build interrupted by a restart is never resumed, only ended `failed`. The spec allows this.
2. Batch budget: the shared pool makes `remaining` the smaller of the build's own and the pool's. A build keeps making cheaper calls while units remain. It does not stop all calls once any single call would not fit. The pool is never exceeded.
3. A `domains` value that is not a list, or an entry that is not a string, is 400 `malformed_request` (§5 default). `null` counts as missing, which is 422.
4. Original pages fetched for a `Canonical` URL count as gathered pages and can yield candidates.
5. A queued batch's builds all start at once, within the outbound-concurrency cap of 48 calls. There is no per-batch build limit.

# Dossier — stage 4

A company-profile service: `POST /dossiers` researches a company by its domain in the
background, through Nimble called via WebRouter, and `GET /dossiers/{domain}` returns seven
fields (the six of stage 1 and `executives`), each with the excerpts that support it and every
candidate value the evidence holds. Stage 3 adds change over time: each value carries
`true_from` and `learned_at`, `GET /dossiers/{domain}?as_of=` answers as the service had the
dossier then, `/values?true_at=` what the evidence says held on a date, `/history` each
field's selected values, and `GET /changes` a feed of every change and correction. State is
kept on disk and survives an abrupt stop. Sources that disagree are ranked by a fixed rule (authority, recency, URL, value);
the best candidate is the field's value and the field is `contested`. Stage 4 adds
`origins` (which independent sources stand behind a value: lineage header lines, lookalike
domains, `corroborated` and `corroborated_since`), an eighth field `investors`, `POST /batches` and
`GET /batches/{id}` (several companies researched under one shared budget), retries when providers
answer with errors, and builds that survive a restart. Researchers use it in
a browser at `/` (list and research form), `/dossiers/{domain}`, `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence`,
`/contested`, `/signup` and `/login`.

    """Units shared by the builds of a batch: together they never spend more than the limit.

    Once a call that a build makes would pass the limit the pool is closed: the batch makes no
    more provider calls (stage 4: Batches), and every build completes with what it has gathered.
    """

    def __init__(self, limit: int):
        self.limit = limit
        self.spent = 0
        self.closed = False
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def take(self, units: int) -> bool:
        with self._lock:
            if self.closed or self.spent + units > self.limit:
                self.closed = True
                return False
            self.spent += units
            return True

    def give_back(self, units: int) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            self.spent -= units

    @property
    def remaining(self) -> int:
        with self._lock:

# Mock web

A local test double for the four provider endpoints a Dossier service calls. It answers as
Nimble, Tavily, Kernel and Browserbase, with their APIs' request and response shapes as
WebRouter 0.12.0, `nimble-python` and `tavily-python` call them, from a corpus of fictional companies
on reserved `.test` domains. There is no internet access and no model behind it: every answer
comes from the corpus files, and the same request against the same corpus and epoch always
gets the same answer.

Use it to develop and check a service offline. The sample corpus in `corpus/sample/` ships
with it.

## Running it

The image reads its corpus from `/data/corpus` and listens on port 8080. It answers each request
on its own thread, with a listen backlog of 128 connections.

```sh
docker build -t dossier-web challenges/dossier/web
docker network create dossier
docker run --rm -d --name web --network dossier \
  -e MOCK_ADMIN_TOKEN=[redacted] \
  -v "$PWD/challenges/dossier/web/corpus/sample:/data/corpus:ro" \
  -p 8080:8080 dossier-web
```

Then start the service on the same network with the provider variables pointing at it:

```sh
docker run --rm --network dossier -p 8000:8000 \
  -e PORT=8000 \
  -e NIMBLE_API_KEY=[redacted] -e NIMBLE_BASE_URL=http://web:8080/nimble \
  -e TAVILY_API_KEY=[redacted] -e TAVILY_BASE_URL=http://web:8080/tavily \
  -e KERNEL_API_KEY=[redacted] -e KERNEL_BASE_URL=http://web:8080/kernel \
  -e BROWSERBASE_API_KEY=[redacted] -e BROWSERBASE_BASE_URL=http://web:8080/browserbase \
  my-dossier-service
```

The keys can be any non-empty string; the mock does not check them. `curl
http://localhost:8080/_mock/health` answers `{"status": "ok"}` once the corpus has loaded.
Without `MOCK_ADMIN_TOKEN` the admin API below is disabled and every admin route answers 404.

**Ledger (stage-4/requirements/LEDGER.md): 383 rows**
- 319 carried from stage 3. Their status is reset to `open (stage 3: passing)`; the 4 `ruled` rows stay ruled.
- 64 new `R4-*` rows, all `open` (test committed, not yet run):
  - R4-GEN 3
  - R4-LIN 2
  - R4-OWN 3

**Rulings (RULINGS.md, RUL-S4-01..26). Ones that change what the service must do:**
- **Own kind:** `own` needs registrant == the company's domain, including for a page with no `Kind` line (it becomes an aggregator).
- **Lookalikes:** a lookalike is an aggregator, and its origin is the company's domain unless First-Published-By or Canonical applies first.
- **Canonical chains:** each page gets its own count of at most 3 follows. The fourth URL's host is the origin, and a missing original's host is the origin. Cycles are cut by the same count.
- **Originals:** a build obtains originals but they are not evidence, so their values are no candidates.
- **Standing origins:** a value or member that leaves and returns starts again. A member field's `corroborated_since` is when every current member reached two origins. `as_of` answers use no later history.
- **Investors:** never `contested`. Non-members are `selected: false` and cited nowhere. Any removed name makes a `change`.
- **Batches:** `domains` of the wrong type is 400. A batch with no build of its own is `done`. A build starved by the budget may end `ready` with every field unknown, or `failed`.

**Acceptance tests** (stage-4/requirements/acceptance/; carried files adapted to eight fields and the new keys)
- `test_s4_lineage` covers lineage, origins and corroboration over 7 builds.
- `test_s4_investors` covers `investors`.
- `test_s4_batches` covers batches: validation, budget, ownership, idempotency, concurrency, 50 domains.
- `test_s4_failure` covers provider failure.
- `test_s4_restart` covers SIGKILL with builds and batches running.
- `test_s4_upgrade` covers stage-1/2/3 exports and the service's own export.
- `test_s4_ui` covers the screens.
- Five new corpus companies plus a `wire-hub.test` pseudo-company that holds only non-searchable originals.

./run.sh --base-url URL --mock-url URL [--old-url U --old2-url U --old3-url U] --container <svc docker name> [pytest args]
python -m pytest test_s4_unit.py test_timeline_unit.py test_rank_unit.py test_oracle_unit.py; python check_corpus.py   # offline, no service
```
- `up.sh` sets `SVC_CONTAINER`, so the restart tests run. Without it they skip. Upgrade tests skip without the old-service URLs.
- Restart tests take about a minute each, and `test_R4_BAT_17` is slow (marked `slow`).
- The new `OLD3_IMAGE` and `--old3-url` options are in `up.sh` and `run.sh`.

@[[8ea258b8-a8ca-45f0-9ebe-2714998424c7]] Items (a) and (b) are done at `91233185b3081619c6eeb68550e03e9d3f86e141` in `stage-4/`. I did not run the harness or any container build, and I have not started (c).

**(a) Batch budget**
- **Behaviour change:** a batch now makes no more provider calls once a call a build makes would pass its budget. The shared `Pool` in `app/providers.py` closes on the first reservation that does not fit.
- **After closing:** every build in the batch sees `remaining == 0`, so no cheaper call is made either. Each build completes with the pages and claims it has already gathered.
- **Prechecks do not close the pool:** the builder's own affordability checks (for example skipping the 25-unit research run when fewer than 25 units remain) only skip that call. The pool closes only when an attempted call does not fit. A tiny budget therefore still yields some evidence.
- **Per-build limit:** a build hitting its own 80-unit limit does not close the batch.

**(b) Provider failure tests**
The new `tests/test_provider_failure.py` has 9 tests. It scripts the provider layer under the real `Gateway` and `Builder` and checks `spent_units == cost of served calls` throughout:
- **Other providers fail:** with every call to the non-nimble providers answered 500, 503 or 429 and Tavily enabled, the build ends `ready` with its fields known.
- **Nimble flaky:** Nimble refuses each call's first two attempts and Tavily always fails. The build still ends `ready`, with spending at most 80.
- **Research always fails:** with every research run answered 500 or 429, the build ends `ready` with all evidence fields known, and the research run is asked again.
- **All providers fail (500):** the build ends `failed` in under 10 s with 0 units spent and 0 served cost.
- **All providers answer 429:** the build ends `failed` with 0 units, and active time (excluding 429 waits) is under 10 s.
- **Extract refusals:** a refused extract for one page only, or for every page, still ends `ready` from the remaining evidence, with refused calls costing 0.
- **Pool closing:** the pool test checks that the first non-fitting reservation closes it and that a refund does not reopen it. A concurrent test of 3 builds sharing a 12-unit pool never exceeds 12 and every build finishes.

**Checks run:** `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` gave 67 tests with 1 failure at `5962` (`59627b5`), in an older pool test that assumed the pre-closing rule. `9123318` updates that test, and `tests.test_stage4` passes 17 of 17 after the change. I did not re-run the full suite after that fix. The provider-failure module takes about 50 s (real 429 waits).

`stage-4/requirements/` is still untracked and not mine.

- **Where the failures are:**
  - **Implementer's fix:** most are lineage and origin mismatches on `linden-forge` and `corvane` (hq_city and founded_year come out contested), plus the stage-3 import tests and `test_R4_RST_05`.   - **Judgement call (2):** I didn't re-probe it on 9123318.
- **Not checked:** restart caps beyond the acceptance restart tests, mid-batch kill, and my own investors and canonical probes.

I'll re-run the harness and acceptance subset when a new revision arrives.

   - linden-forge's candidate set holds a Graz candidate from copycat.test (kind `news`, origin linden-forge.test) and a Vienna one, but lacks the oracle's second Graz candidate. This is probably a lookalike/own or original-page candidate issue.

- Judgement call (2): on 373f10f the builder picks cheaper calls to fit the remaining budget. 9123318 closes the pool on the first non-fitting reservation; the acceptance budget tests pass on it, but I did not re-probe.
- Provider failure (mock faults), 373f10f only, on the sample corpus:

  - Nimble research error / 429: ready, 7 known.
  - Nimble research+extract error: ready in 4.3s, 7 known.

  - Nimble search alone failing is not a spec'd scenario: tavily search remained reachable, and the spec wording is "every call to one or more providers fails". Not blocking.
  - All providers error: `failed` in 6.1s with 0 units, which is inside the 10s bound.
  - Failed calls cost 0 (errcost=0 in every run).

**Next step:** Implementer should fix items 1-3, and the Analyst should adjudicate item 4 and the `retrieved_at` question in item 2. Send me a new revision and I will re-run the harness and the acceptance subset, and probe investors and canonical myself.

**(B) `test_R4_BAT_05` — test fix, not a defect**
- The two nimble extract calls were matched because the test looked for any URL containing the existing domain.
- I did not inspect which URLs they fetched. The spec only requires that the batch not research the existing domain and that it cost nothing, and an extract of a talloway URL is not that: another company's search can return it.
- The test now looks only for searches or research runs whose query names talloway. It also asserts the talloway dossier body is byte-for-byte unchanged (fields, `spent_units`, `researched_at`). It uses `RUL-S4-27`.
- If the unchanged-body assertion fails, that is a defect. The Implementer should check that those extracts are not for TAL itself.

**(C) `UPG_06` and `UPG_07` — both test bugs, fixed**
- `UPG_06` hit a `KeyError` in my own helper: the stage-3 bodies have no `investors`. I made it tolerate that.
- `UPG_07` hit a `KeyError` because the first `/values` pair for quillon used an `as_of` before its first build, so the stage-3 service answered 404 too. I used valid pairs per domain and assert the old answer was a 200.
- `UPG_06` does not expect imported candidates to have `retrieved_at` equal to the build time, beyond "answer as the stage-3 service did". It compares each `as_of` candidate with the old `as_of` candidate, `retrieved_at` included, minus the new `origin` key.
- For `corroborated_since` the spec needs only gathered-at semantics: "When a stage-3 export is imported, the candidates of each of its builds count as gathered at that build's time". It does not require `retrieved_at` changes.

**One more failure — `RST_05`: implementation defect**
- `test_R4_RST_05` (interrupted refresh). After the restart the dossier ended `ready`, yet `researched_at` and every candidate's `retrieved_at` were still the earlier build's time (2026-03-01, not the refresh's 2026-03-06). The fields were the old build's.
- I inferred this from the log; I did not read the code.
- The spec sentences: §8 says `researched_at` is "the time of the last build that completed `ready`". Stage-4 Restarts says the build "ends `ready` or `failed` … It may end `failed` although some of its calls succeeded; it then leaves the fields as they were."
- `ready` means the build completed, so its fields and time must be the new build's. Leaving the old fields is only allowed with `failed`. The test is right.
- The Implementer should end such a build `failed` or complete it properly.

**Defect list for the Implementer:**
1. Originals as candidates (A).
2. `RST_05`: an interrupted refresh must not end `ready` with the old fields and old `researched_at`.

**Tests the Reviewer should re-run after both fixes:** the full stage-4 subset, with `ORG_02` and `RST_05` as the gates.

The new revision is `bf368e7279a4b00c0beaf0f07e61e9e48a4a8324`. The full unit suite passes (67 of 67, 88 s), and I did not run the harness. I sent the report to the coordinator.

**Acceptance run:** I ran the acceptance suite as of `ba751ed` against code at `b5c0164`, selecting only the stage-4 tests (`-k R4_`). It ended with 94 passed, 2 failed, 10 skipped. The skipped ones need the stage-1 and stage-2 images. I ran `up.sh` three times for this adjudication, and the containers are removed.

**Fixes:**
- **Originals are not evidence:** a page fetched only to resolve an origin yields no candidates or page versions. I also found the originals were being fetched too late, after the 80-unit budget went to noise pages. They are now resolved at the end of each gather step.
- **Interrupted builds:** after a restart, a build that was running now sets the dossier to `failed` with the last ready fields kept.
- **Existing dossiers in a batch:** they are not researched and their body is unchanged. `test_R4_BAT_05` passed in the run.

**The two failures:** `test_R4_COR_06` and `test_R4_COR_07` get 401 because `test_R4_ORG_02` resets the service in the middle of a module that shares one signed-in fixture. I flagged this to the coordinator for the Analyst, since it looks like a test-order problem rather than a service bug. I did not confirm that by running them in isolation.

I also fixed a race in my own restart unit test.

@[[8ea258b8-a8ca-45f0-9ebe-2714998424c7]] New revision `bf368e7279a4b00c0beaf0f07e61e9e48a4a8324` in `stage-4/`. The full unit suite passes (67 of 67, 88 s). Against the acceptance tests as of `ba751ed`, my last targeted run passed 94 and failed 2 (COR_06/07), both a test-order defect (below). I did not run the harness.

**Fixes (commits `42fd288`, `b5c0164`, `bf368e7`)**
1. **Originals are not evidence (the ORG/OWN/COR/UI_02/FAIL group):**
   - **Rule applied:** a page extracted only to resolve an origin still feeds origin resolution but yields no candidates and no page version.
   - **Exception:** a page that a search returned or a research claim cited stays evidence.
   - **Second cause (`b5c0164`):** originals were being fetched too late. On `oakhurst-media.test` the 80-unit budget went to noise pages first, so the original was never obtained and the origin fell back to the URL's host. Originals are now resolved at the end of every `_gather`, before further pages are read.
2. **RST_05:** after a restart, an interrupted build now sets the dossier state to `failed` with the last ready fields kept. Previously I kept `ready` alongside the old `researched_at`.
3. **BAT_05 and the unchanged-dossier check:** for a domain that already has a dossier, the batch makes no provider call and leaves the dossier unchanged. BAT_05 passed in the run below.

**Acceptance run, as of `ba751ed` and `b5c0164`**
I ran `up.sh --build` with `SUFFIX=impl`, `OLD3_IMAGE` set to a locally built stage-3 image, and `-k "R4_"`. It used private ports and containers, which `up.sh` removed afterwards. That run had **94 passed, 2 failed, 10 skipped**. The skips are the UPG tests that need the stage-1 and stage-2 images.
- **Passed:** every BAT test, including BAT_05 and BAT_16, plus FAIL, investors, lineage OWN/ORG, RST, UI and UPG_06/07 (the stage-3 import tests).
- **Failed:** `test_R4_COR_06` and `test_R4_COR_07`, both a test-order defect, not the service.

**Test-order defect for the Analyst**
`test_R4_ORG_02` uses the `fresh` fixture, which resets the service, and it sits in the middle of `test_s4_lineage.py`, where all the other tests share the module-scoped `world` fixture. COR_06/07 run after it, so `world`'s bearer token is gone and they get 401 `unknown token`. Moving ORG_02 to the end of the file, or giving it its own service state, fixes it. Before ORG_02 was rewritten, COR_06/07 passed in my earlier subset run.

I also fixed a race in my own restart unit test (`bf368e7`); it had failed once in 4 full runs.

I ran `up.sh` three times for this adjudication: two targeted runs and one full `R4_` run. I also ran a manual mock plus service pair with the corpus to read the mock call log.
